hero.title: Run your coding agents side by side, and see what each one is doing.
hero.lede: trace is a desktop app for Claude Code and Codex. Start an agent on a ticket or a quick idea; each gets its own git worktree, and you follow them all from one calm window: chat, files, terminal, inbox and fleet.
hero.alt: trace showing an agent's chat on the left, the files it changed with their diff on the right, and a terminal below running the tests: three passing.

features.label: Agents as a chat
features.title: Claude and Codex, as a conversation you can read
features.text: Agents run as a formatted chat rather than a wall of terminal output: Markdown replies, a card per tool call, the diff of every edit, and permission prompts answered right where they appear.
points: Claude Code and Codex, in chat or in their own terminal
Tool runs fold into one line once a turn ends
Allow once, always, or deny, without leaving the conversation
features.alt: A prompt asks the agent to add a delete() helper and a test. Read cards appear for the files it looks at, then an edit waits for permission; Allow once is clicked, the diff appears, the tests run, and the agent replies in Markdown that all three tests pass.

features.label: Subagents
features.title: Subagents get live cards, their own tabs, and a pane beside you
features.text: When an agent fans work out, each subagent shows as a live card with its state, tool count and time. Open one in its own tab, or beside the chat to watch its brief, calls and report come in.
points: Background subagents keep the agent working, and stoppable
Each subagent's brief and report, in full
Stop one without stopping the rest
features.alt: The agent starts two subagents in parallel. Two cards show them running; one is opened beside the chat, where its brief, a Read call and then its finished report appear while the other card turns to Done.

features.label: Split panes
features.title: Chat, Files and Terminal, arranged like an IDE
features.text: Every agent's tabs can sit side by side or stacked: the conversation, the files it changed, and a shell in the same worktree. Layouts are remembered per workspace.
points: Split right, split down, or move a tab to the next pane
Files shows the changes against the base branch, with diffs
A plain shell rooted in the agent's worktree
features.alt: From a single chat pane, Files is split to the right and Terminal moved below it. A shell opens in the agent's worktree, npm test runs and passes, and the changed test file's diff is shown.

features.label: Board and ticket agents
features.title: Start an agent from a Jira or Pylon ticket
features.text: Connect Jira, Pylon or both, and each adds its board to the sidebar exactly as your tracker shows it. Start work on a card and trace opens an agent in a new worktree for that ticket; moves sync back to the tracker. Everything else works with no tracker at all.
points: Your board's own columns, filters and sprints
Dragging a card to in progress starts its agent
GitHub sign-in to browse and clone your repos
features.alt: trace's Integrations page with three cards: Jira, Pylon and GitHub.
features.caption: Shown without a tracker connected: no ticket data is made up for this page.

features.label: Sessions and worktrees
features.title: Every agent in its own worktree, and you can see who started it
features.text: Sessions are agents that aren't tied to a ticket. Each runs in its own git worktree of a repo you've added, or in any folder. Lists sort by status, name, age or who started them, or keep your own order.
points: Started by you, another agent, the orchestrator or a schedule
Sections and drag to reorder
Branch and diff counts on every row
features.alt: The Sessions list is sorted by who started each session, which nests a session another agent started under that agent's session, then by status, then back to manual order. The agent-started session is opened, showing its repo, worktree branch and who started it.

features.label: Inbox
features.title: One inbox for every question and approval
features.text: When any agent needs you, it lands in the Inbox with its question or the exact change it wants to make. Answer it there and the agent carries on; you don't have to find its tab first.
points: Questions with options, or your own answer
Approvals with the full command or edit
Notifications and an optional sound
features.alt: The Inbox lists agents that need you. A question about default units is answered with Metric, then an agent's edit adding a --json flag is approved, and the next request arrives.

features.label: Fleet
features.title: Every running agent at a glance
features.text: Fleet is a table of every live agent: its state, how long it's been there, its repo and branch, changes, PR and latest line. Rows stay put when an agent changes state, so you never lose your place.
points: Filter by Needs you, Working or Ready
Opened order, or drag to reorder
The latest thing each agent said
features.alt: The Fleet table with five agents: some Ready, two needing you and one Working. Filters for Needs you and Working are tried, and the working agent finishes while its row stays in place.

features.label: Orchestrator
features.title: Ask what your agents are doing
features.text: The orchestrator sits in the side panel and knows your board and sessions. Ask it for a status round-up, what's blocked, or to nudge an agent; every action it takes waits for your confirm. Stats chart your agents and their work.
points: Your API key, or your logged-in Claude CLI
Charts of agents by state, and session stats
Actions behind a confirm card
features.alt: The orchestrator is asked what the agents are doing. It replies with who needs you, which agents are ready and a chart of agents by state, then its Stats tab is opened.

features.label: Scheduled prompts
features.title: Prompts that run themselves, when there's something to do
features.text: Run a prompt every few minutes, daily, weekly, monthly or on a cron expression, each run in a fresh worktree. A precheck command decides whether a run goes ahead, so a nightly job can skip the nights nothing changed.
points: Variables like {lastRunAt}, {date} and {repo}
Run history with each run's conversation
Import and export prompts to share them
features.alt: A new scheduled prompt called Morning test run is filled in: a prompt, a daily schedule, allowed tools and a precheck command that only runs it when the branch is behind. It's saved and its detail shows the precheck.

features.label: Files and Quick Open
features.title: Find any file in the worktree in a keystroke
features.text: The Files tab shows the worktree's tree and what the agent changed. Quick Open fuzzy-searches the whole worktree, and opens a file in the Files tab or in your own editor.
points: Changes or all files, with filters
Quick Open: Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows and Linux, ⌘P on macOS
Open in your editor from any file
features.alt: In an agent's Files tab, All files shows the worktree's tree and a file is opened. Quick Open is then brought up, a few letters narrow it to router.test.ts, and Enter opens that file with its diff.

features.label: Terminal extras
features.title: A terminal that knows what it's showing
features.text: Find in the scrollback, a menu on links and file paths (open, copy, open in editor), and Copy Context, which copies the selection or the last 100 lines headed with the agent and worktree, ready to paste into another agent.
points: Find: Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, ⌘F on macOS
Right-click for the same menu
Copy Context for handing work between agents
features.alt: In an agent's shell, git status lists the two changed files. Right-clicking a file path opens a menu with Open in VS Code, IntelliJ or Cursor, Show in folder, Copy path, Copy context and Find; Find then highlights each match for router in the scrollback.

features.label: Make it yours
features.title: Themes, fonts, density, sidebar and shortcuts
features.text: Dark, Light, Midnight, Paper or System, an accent colour, interface size and density, fonts for the UI, terminal and chat, each with a live preview. Order and hide the sidebar's pages, rebind every shortcut, and press ? for the cheat sheet.
points: Live previews while you choose
Terminal schemes and cursor styles
Every shortcut rebindable, shown in menus and the cheat sheet
features.alt: Settings → Appearance: the theme switches from Dark to Light, Paper and Midnight and back, with the previews updating; the accent and density change; then the Sidebar settings and the keyboard shortcut cheat sheet open.
